question.problem: Using the standard form of the Maclaurin series of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion of the definite integral ${\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\sqrt{x})\,\text{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
The power series expansion of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is given by

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=x-\frac{1}{6}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{120}{x}^{5}+⋯\,.
$$

Replacing $x$ with $2\sqrt{x}$ in the above, we get

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\sqrt{x})=2\sqrt{x}-\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{{x}^{3}}+\frac{4}{15}\sqrt{{x}^{5}}+⋯\,.
$$

Now, we multiply the series by $\sqrt{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\sqrt{x}) & =\sqrt{x}(2\sqrt{x}-\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{{x}^{3}}+\frac{4}{15}\sqrt{{x}^{5}}+⋯) \\  & =2x-\frac{4{x}^{2}}{3}+\frac{4{x}^{3}}{15}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\sqrt{x})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2x-\frac{4{x}^{2}}{3}+\frac{4{x}^{3}}{15}+⋯)\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}-\frac{4{x}^{3}}{9}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{15}+⋯){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & ={\pi }^{2}-\frac{4{\pi }^{3}}{9}+\frac{{\pi }^{4}}{15}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$
